title: Java script question
summary: Q&A on using external data; tg_jp supplies Wave Loader.js, a Tool script that reads a .wav file and builds splines of the waveform.

evidence.author: tg_jp
evidence.quote: .wav format seems to be simple binary format. so you can read directly via javascript of Cheetah3D.

evidence.quote: I tried the wave loader script but the spline it produced looked very different.

evidence.author: tg_jp
evidence.quote: I fixed bug when 16 bit .wav file.

evidence.author: frank beckmann
evidence.quote: Looking good now.

api_lessons: Binary files can be read in JS: new File(path); file.open(READ_MODE, LITTLE_ENDIAN); file.read(n) returns a string; file.seek(off, SEEK_SET|SEEK_CUR); file.close().
The fixed loader uses file.readInt() for 16-bit samples and readShort() for header fields; readInt is not in the 8.1.1 File docs (documented: readShort/readUInt/readFloat).
Interop with external programs is possible via OS.system() plus exchanging data through temp files (slow but works).
notes: Original (2009) version mis-read 16-bit WAVs; use the 2010-09-02 version. Exotic WAV variants (e.g. 32-bit float) may not parse.

title: Debugging Types in Cheetah3D
summary: Helper scripts mapping numeric type/family/tag/parameter constants back to names, and dumping an object's parameters and tags.

evidence.author: Reshka
evidence.quote: the docs do not map the numbers to the types.

evidence.author: Edward
evidence.quote: Neat- I wrote something similar just the other day

api_lessons: obj.type(), obj.family(), tag.type(), parameter.type() return numbers; compare with global constants (POLYGONOBJ, NGONFAMILY, PROPWINTAG, FLOAT_PARAMETER, ...). Constants collide across groups, so name lookup needs context.
All constants are numeric properties of the global object; enumerate with for(p in (function(){return this;})()) to build a reverse map.
Introspection: obj.parameterCount()/parameterAtIndex(i) -> parameter.name()/type(); obj.tagCount()/tagAtIndex(i); then obj.getParameter(name).
Edward found SPOTLIGHT, DISTANTLIGHT, AREALIGHT constants missing (2012); UVTAG commented out.
notes: Two independent utilities: Reshka's ConstMap (post 74880) and Edward's object/tag parameter dumper (post 74936).

evidence.quote: Thanks Martin! That works perfectly.

api_lessons: In v7+ render resolution lives on the renderer, not the camera: doc.currentRenderer().setParameter("resolution", new Vec2D(x,y)). Camera resolutionX/resolutionY are legacy.
Renderers: doc.currentRenderer() or doc.rendererAtIndex(i).
addParameterSelector returns the selected index from getParameter; parameter names must be unique per tool or selectors share state.
Pre-v7: camera = doc.activeCamera(); camera.getParameter("resolutionX"/"resolutionY"). Use Macro 'Parameter Info.js' or developer mode tooltips to discover parameter names.
notes: Pre-v7 version 'Camera Aspect Ratio.js' worked on 6.x. Thread also has podperson's searchChildren() recursive helper and an Object-Info documentation script.

title: Converting Cheetah's uvcoords to tverts
summary: Q&A while writing a Neverwinter Nights MDL exporter: mapping per-corner UV coords to shared tverts.

evidence.author: aaronparr
evidence.quote: as a workaround I have expressly compared each property of the two Vec4D and the code is working.

evidence.author: aaronparr
evidence.quote: I can view a model in the neverwinternights game produced by Cheetah3d.

api_lessons: UVs are per polygon corner: core.uvCoord(pindex, cornerIndex) returns Vec4D (x=U, y=V); dedupe them yourself to build a shared tvert list.
Triangulation: core.triangleCount(); for each polygon, triangles 0..polygonSize-3 via core.triangle(pindex, t) returning 3 corner indices; map to vertices with core.vertexIndex(pindex, corner).
Vec4D.isEqual(otherVec4D) threw 'Wrong number or type of arguments' in practice (2015); compare x/y/z/w manually.
notes: Full exporter script was on pastebin (http://pastebin.com/WXZBFF2p).
